findings.title: [P1] Reject NaN, Infinity, fractional, and unsafe timeout values
findings.body: `Number(value)` returns `NaN` for any non-numeric string, and `NaN <= 0` evaluates to `false`, so the validation passes and `NaN` is returned as a timeout (`src/options.ts:11-12`). The same hole admits `"Infinity"` and `"1e309"` (→ `Infinity`), `"1.5"` (→ 1.5), and `"9007199254740993"` (unsafe integer). The removed `!Number.isSafeInteger(timeout)` guard previously rejected every one of these with `"invalid timeout"`. A validation function whose entire purpose is to reject bad input now silently accepts it, and the poison values propagate: `NaN` defeats all downstream numeric comparisons, and Node's `setTimeout` coerces `NaN`/`Infinity` delays to 1 ms, making deadlines fire immediately instead of the configuration error surfacing. Restore a guard equivalent to `Number.isSafeInteger(timeout) && timeout > 0` (or `Number.isFinite` plus an integer check).

findings.title: [P2] Preserve base-10 parseInt semantics for accepted input forms
findings.body: `Number()` accepts and reinterprets string forms that `Number.parseInt(value, 10)` did not (`src/options.ts:11`): `"0x10"` now returns 16 (previously threw, since radix-10 parsing yields 0), `"1e3"` now returns 1000 (previously 1, because `parseInt` stopped at `e`), `"1.5"` now returns 1.5 (previously 1), and `"12ms"` now returns `NaN` (previously 12). Even after restoring a safe-integer guard, these interpretation changes remain and contradict the PR's stated goal of "preserving existing contracts". Either keep `Number.parseInt(value, 10)` for identical accepted-input semantics, or deliberately document the new accepted grammar (whole-string numeric, including exponent/hex forms).

findings.title: [P3] Add tests covering the changed parsing contract
findings.body: `parseTimeout` is exported but has no tests (and no current callers) in the repository, so the rewritten validation has no executable specification. A small table-driven test over `undefined`, valid positive integers, zero/negative, non-numeric strings, non-finite strings (`"Infinity"`, `"1e309"`), fractional, and prefix-garbage inputs (`"12ms"`) would have caught the P1 regression and would lock the intended contract for future changes.
